summary: Kodesh, the food of korbanos, has stricter rules of tahara than terumah. This mishnah lists some of those stricter rules.

chunks.en: Kodesh has stricter rules than terumah:
chunks.st: Concerning several matters there is greater stringency with regard to sacrificial food than with regard to teruma,
chunks.stMore: a portion of the produce designated for the priest.

words.note: A gift of food for the Kohanim.

chunks.en: for terumah we may tovel keilim inside other keilim,
chunks.st: This expresses itself in many ways, the first being that one may immerse vessels inside other vessels to purify them for teruma;

words.note: Dip in a mikveh to make tahor.

chunks.en: but not for kodesh.
chunks.st: but not for sacrificial food,
chunks.stMore: for which one must immerse each vessel separately.

chunks.en: For terumah, the outside, inside and handle of a kli count as separate parts,
chunks.explain: If one part becomes tamei, the other parts stay tahor.
chunks.st: Another difference is that the halakhot of the back of a vessel and its inside and its place for gripping apply to vessels used for teruma,
chunks.stMore: meaning that each part of the vessel has its own use and is considered a separate vessel in that it does not convey impurity to the other parts of the vessel when it contracts impurity;

words.note: The handle, where you hold the kli.

chunks.en: but not for kodesh.
chunks.st: but not to sacrificial food,
chunks.stMore: for which an impure section of the vessel does convey impurity to all the other sections.

chunks.he: הַנּוֹשֵׂא אֶת הַמִּדְרָס נוֹשֵׂא אֶת הַתְּרוּמָה,
chunks.en: Someone carrying something with midras tumah may also carry terumah,
chunks.st: Likewise, one who carries an object trodden on by a zav, a man suffering from gonorrhea, may carry teruma
chunks.stMore: at the same time, if he is careful that neither he nor the impure object should come into contact with the teruma,

words.note: Something with a strong kind of tumah, like a seat a zav sat on.

chunks.en: but not kodesh.
chunks.st: but this may not be done with sacrificial food.

chunks.en: The clothes of those who eat terumah
chunks.st: The garments of those who eat teruma

chunks.en: are counted as midras for kodesh.
chunks.st: are like an object trodden on by a zav with regard to sacrificial food.

chunks.en: The rule of terumah is not like the rule of kodesh:
chunks.st: The mishna lists other stringencies that apply to sacrificial foods but not to teruma: The characteristics of teruma are not like the characteristics of sacrificial food,

chunks.en: for kodesh, he unties a knot, dries it, and tovels it,
chunks.explain: A knot or wetness could keep the mikveh water from reaching everywhere.
chunks.st: as in the case of vessels that are used with sacrificial food, if one has a garment or vessel that is tied up he must untie it and dry it if there was any moisture on it,
chunks.stMore: as both a knot and absorbed moisture are considered interpositions that prevent the water of the ritual bath from reaching the entire garment.

chunks.en: and only after that ties it again;
chunks.st: And he may then immerse them, and afterward he may tie them up again if he wishes.

chunks.en: but for terumah, he may tie it and then tovel it.
chunks.st: But with regard to teruma he may, if he so desires, tie up the garment and then immerse it without any concern that the knot might be considered an interposition.

summary: More stricter rules for kodesh than for terumah: about new keilim, food in one kli, levels of tumah, and tamei hands.

chunks.en: Keilim that were finished being made while tahor
chunks.st: Vessels that were fashioned and completed in purity

chunks.en: must be toveled before using them for kodesh,
chunks.st: nevertheless require immersion to be considered pure for sacrificial foods,

chunks.en: but not for terumah.
chunks.st: but not for teruma.

chunks.en: A kli joins together all the food inside it for kodesh,
chunks.explain: If one piece becomes tamei, all the pieces become tamei.
chunks.st: A vessel combines all the food that is in it with regard to sacrificial food,
chunks.stMore: meaning that if one piece of food becomes impure all the other pieces become impure as well;

chunks.en: but not for terumah.
chunks.st: but not with regard to teruma,
chunks.stMore: concerning which each piece is treated independently.

chunks.en: Kodesh can become pasul even at the fourth level of tumah,
chunks.explain: Tumah passes from thing to thing in steps, called levels.
chunks.st: The mishna continues the list of differences between sacrificial food and teruma. Sacrificial food that is impure with fourth-degree impurity is disqualified,
chunks.stMore: meaning that the sacrificial food is rendered impure but it does not impart impurity to other items.

words.note: The fourth level, or step, of tumah.

chunks.en: but terumah only up to the third level.
chunks.st: Teruma is disqualified when it is impure with third-degree impurity;
chunks.stMore: it is not susceptible to fourth-degree impurity at all.

chunks.en: And for terumah, if one of his hands became tamei,
chunks.st: And with regard to teruma, if one of one’s hands became impure
chunks.stMore: by rabbinic law that renders only the hands impure,

chunks.en: the other hand is still tahor.
chunks.st: its counterpart, i.e., the other hand, remains pure.

chunks.en: But for kodesh, he must tovel both hands,
chunks.st: But with regard to sacrificial food, if one hand becomes impure he must immerse them both,

chunks.en: because one hand makes the other hand tamei for kodesh,
chunks.st: as one hand renders its counterpart impure with regard to sacrificial food

chunks.en: but not for terumah.
chunks.st: but not with regard to teruma.

summary: More differences between kodesh and terumah: about eating dry food with tamei hands, and about people who must go to the mikveh before eating kodesh.

chunks.he: אוֹכְלִין אֳכָלִים נְגוּבִין בְּיָדַיִם מְסֹאָבוֹת בַּתְּרוּמָה,
chunks.en: We may eat dry foods with tamei hands when it is terumah,
chunks.st: One may eat dry foods, i.e., foods that have never come into contact with liquid and are therefore not susceptible to impurity, with impure hands when it is teruma,

chunks.en: but not when it is kodesh.
chunks.st: but not when it is sacrificial food.

chunks.en: An onen and someone who still has to bring a korban to finish becoming tahor
chunks.st: An acute mourner [onen], i.e., someone who has experienced the loss of a close relative on that day, who had not come into contact with the deceased; and one who is lacking atonement, i.e., someone who still needs to bring an offering to complete his purification procedure, such as a zav or a woman after childbirth,

words.note: Someone whose close relative died that day.
Someone who still needs to bring a korban to finish becoming tahor.

chunks.en: must go to the mikveh before eating kodesh,
chunks.st: both require immersion in order to eat sacrificial food.
chunks.stMore: The onen would immerse after the day has passed and the one lacking atonement would immerse after the requisite offering is brought.

chunks.en: but not before eating terumah.
chunks.st: However, immersion in these cases is not necessary for eating teruma.

summary: Terumah also has some stricter rules than kodesh. People who are not careful about tahara are believed about kodesh all year, but about terumah only at the time of making wine and oil.
stIntro: The previous mishna listed stringencies that apply to sacrificial food but not to teruma. However, there are also

chunks.en: Terumah is stricter in this way:
chunks.st: stringencies that apply to teruma over sacrificial food:

chunks.en: In Yehudah, everyone is believed that wine
chunks.explain: Even an am ha'aretz, who is not careful about tumah.
chunks.st: In Judea all people, even people who are not generally meticulous in their observance of the halakhot of ritual purity [amei ha’aretz], are trusted with regard to the purity of consecrated wine

chunks.en: and oil for the Beis HaMikdash are tahor, all year long.
chunks.st: and oil throughout all the days of the year.

chunks.he: וּבִשְׁעַת הַגִּתּוֹת וְהַבַּדִּים אַף עַל הַתְּרוּמָה.
chunks.en: And at the time of making wine and oil, they are believed even about terumah.
chunks.explain: Then everyone makes his keilim tahor.
chunks.st: And during the period of the winepress and olive press, when grapes and olives are pressed and made into wine and oil, respectively, they are trusted even with regard to the purity of teruma,
chunks.stMore: as all people, including amei ha’aretz, purify their vessels for this season.

chunks.en: If the time of making wine and oil passed, and someone brought a Kohen
chunks.st: But once the periods of the winepress and olive press have passed, if amei ha’aretz brought to him, i.e., to a priest who is meticulous concerning the halakhot of ritual purity [ḥaver],

chunks.en: a barrel of terumah wine,
chunks.st: a barrel of teruma wine,

chunks.en: the Kohen should not take it from him.
chunks.st: he may not accept it from them,
chunks.stMore: as amei ha’aretz are not trusted with regard to matters of ritual purity during the rest of the year.

chunks.en: But he may leave it for the next wine-making time.
chunks.st: But the giver may leave it over for the following winepress season,
chunks.stMore: in the following year, at which point the ḥaver priest may accept it from him, although it was prohibited for him to accept the same barrel beforehand.

chunks.en: And if he told the Kohen,
chunks.st: And if the giver said to the priest:

chunks.en: "I put a revi'is of kodesh into it," he is believed.
chunks.explain: He is believed about kodesh, so also about the terumah with it.
chunks.st: I separated and placed into this barrel of teruma a quarter-log of sacrificial wine or oil, he is trusted
chunks.stMore: with regard to the entire contents of the barrel. Since an am ha’aretz is trusted with regard to the purity of sacrificial food, he is also believed with regard to teruma that is mingled with the sacrificial food.

words.note: A small measure, about a cup.

chunks.en: Jugs of wine and jugs of oil that have terumah mixed in:
chunks.st: With regard to jugs of wine and jugs of oil that are mingled,

chunks.en: people are believed about them at the time of making wine and oil,
chunks.st: amei ha’aretz are trusted with regard to them during the period of the winepress and the olive press,

chunks.en: and for seventy days before the wine-making time.
chunks.st: and also up to seventy days before the winepress,
chunks.stMore: for that is when people begin to purify their vessels in preparation for the wine-pressing season.

summary: Near Yerushalayim, up to the town of Modi'im, every potter is believed that his clay pots are tahor. Farther away, a potter who is not careful is not believed.

chunks.en: From Modi'im and in, toward Yerushalayim,
chunks.st: From Modi’im and inward toward Jerusalem,
chunks.stMore: i.e., in the area surrounding Jerusalem, up to the distance of the town of Modi’im, which is fifteen mil from Jerusalem,

words.note: A town fifteen mil from Yerushalayim.

chunks.en: potters are believed about clay keilim.
chunks.st: all potters, including amei ha’aretz, are deemed credible with regard to the purity of earthenware vessels that they have produced.
chunks.stMore: Because these places supplied earthenware vessels for the people in Jerusalem, the Sages did not decree impurity for them.

chunks.en: From Modi'im and farther out,
chunks.st: From Modi’im and outward, however,

chunks.en: they are not believed.
chunks.st: they are not deemed credible.

chunks.en: How is this? A potter who sells pots
chunks.st: The details of this ruling are specified: How so? A potter who sells pots,

chunks.en: came in past Modi'im:
chunks.st: if he entered within Modi’im from outside it,

chunks.he: הוּא הַקַּדָּר וְהֵן הַקְּדֵרוֹת וְהֵן הַלּוֹקְחִים, נֶאֱמָן.
chunks.en: the same potter, the same pots and the same buyers, he is believed.
chunks.explain: Even though they all came from outside Modi'im.
chunks.st: although the potter, and the pots, and the customers were all previously located outside Modi’im, where he is not deemed credible with regard to purity, he is now deemed credible.

chunks.en: If he went out, he is not believed.
chunks.st: And the opposite is true of the opposite case: If the same person who was deemed credible inside left the boundaries of Modi’im, he is no longer deemed credible.

summary: Tax collectors or thieves who say they did not touch anything are believed. In Yerushalayim everyone is believed about kodesh, and on Yom Tov even about terumah.

chunks.en: Tax collectors who came into a house,
chunks.st: In the case of amei ha’aretz tax collectors who entered a house to collect items for a tax,

chunks.en: and also thieves who brought back the keilim,
chunks.st: and similarly thieves who returned the vessels they had stolen,

chunks.en: are believed when they say,
chunks.st: they are deemed credible when they say:

chunks.en: "We did not touch the other things."
chunks.st: We did not touch
chunks.stMore: the rest of the objects in the house, and those items remain pure.

chunks.en: And in Yerushalayim everyone is believed about kodesh,
chunks.st: And in Jerusalem all people, even amei ha’aretz, are deemed credible with regard to sacrificial food throughout the year,

chunks.en: and at the time of the Yom Tov, even about terumah.
chunks.st: and during a pilgrimage Festival they are deemed credible even with regard to teruma.

words.note: The Yom Tov when everyone came to Yerushalayim.

summary: During Yom Tov everyone is counted as tahor, so after Yom Tov the keilim of the Beis HaMikdash were made tahor again. The mishnah also says when this was done.

chunks.en: Someone who opens his barrel of wine to sell,
chunks.st: In the case of one who opens his barrel of wine for public sale,

chunks.en: or starts selling his dough during Yom Tov,
chunks.explain: People who are not careful about tahara touched it.
chunks.st: and similarly one who starts selling his dough during the time of the pilgrimage Festival, and these items perforce come into contact with amei ha’aretz,

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says: he may finish selling it after Yom Tov.
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says: Since the food was pure, despite its contact with amei ha’aretz, when he began selling it, he may finish selling it in a state of purity even after the Festival,
chunks.stMore: and there is no concern about the contact that has been made by amei ha’aretz during the Festival.

chunks.en: And the Sages say: he may not finish.
chunks.st: But the Rabbis say: He may not finish selling it.

chunks.en: Once Yom Tov was over,
chunks.st: Once the pilgrimage Festival has passed by,

chunks.en: they would make the keilim of the Azarah tahor again.
chunks.explain: Many people had touched them during Yom Tov.
chunks.st: the priests pass all the vessels of the Temple courtyard through a process of purification,
chunks.stMore: since they were touched by am ha’aretz priests during the Festival.

words.note: The courtyard of the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: If Yom Tov ended and the next day was Friday,
chunks.st: If the Festival passed by into a Friday, i.e., if the Festival ended on Thursday night,

chunks.en: they would not do it then,
chunks.st: they would not pass the vessels through the purification process on that day,

chunks.en: because of the honor of Shabbos.
chunks.st: due to the honor of Shabbat,
chunks.stMore: in order to give the priests time to prepare the requirements of Shabbat.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: Not even on Thursday,
chunks.st: They do not even purify them on Thursday,
chunks.stMore: in the event that the Festival ended on Wednesday night,

chunks.en: because the Kohanim are not free.
chunks.st: because the priests are not free to do so.

summary: This mishnah tells how they made the keilim of the Beis HaMikdash tahor after Yom Tov. There were extra keilim, so one could be used while another was being toveled.

chunks.en: How did they make the Azarah tahor?
chunks.st: How do they pass all the vessels of the Temple courtyard through a process of purification?

chunks.en: They toveled the keilim that were in the Beis HaMikdash.
chunks.st: They immerse the vessels that were in the Temple.

chunks.en: And during Yom Tov they would say to the people,
chunks.st: And they say to the am ha’aretz priests who served in the Temple during the Festival:

chunks.he: הִזָּהֲרוּ שֶׁלֹּא תִגְּעוּ בַּשֻּׁלְחָן וּבַמְּנוֹרָה וּתְטַמְּאוּהוּ.
chunks.en: "Be careful not to touch the Shulchan and the Menorah and make them tamei."
chunks.explain: The Shulchan always had to have the lechem hapanim on it.
chunks.st: Be careful that you not touch the table of the shewbread.
chunks.stMore: If you defile it by touching it, it would need to be removed for immersion, and this would lead to the temporary suspension of the mitzva of the shewbread, which had to be on the table at all times.
chunks.basisNote: Steinsaltz's English mentions only the table; the Hebrew also names the Menorah.

words.note: The golden table for the lechem hapanim.

chunks.en: All the keilim that were in the Beis HaMikdash
chunks.st: The mishna continues: All the vessels that were in the Temple

chunks.en: had a second and a third set,
chunks.st: had second and third substitute vessels,

chunks.en: so that if the first ones became tamei,
chunks.st: so that if the first ones became impure

chunks.en: they could bring the second ones instead.
chunks.st: they could bring the second ones in their place.

chunks.en: All the keilim that were in the Beis HaMikdash
chunks.st: All the vessels that were in the Temple

chunks.en: needed tevilah after Yom Tov,
chunks.st: required immersion after the Festival,

chunks.en: except the golden mizbe'ach and the copper mizbe'ach,
chunks.st: apart from the golden altar and the bronze altar,

chunks.en: because they are like the ground.
chunks.st: because they are considered like the ground
chunks.stMore: and therefore, like land itself, not susceptible to impurity.

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Eliezer says.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Eliezer.

chunks.en: And the Sages say:
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: It is because they are covered with metal.
chunks.st: It is because they are coated.
